question.problem:
Which of the following statements are logically equivalent?

I. $¬Q∧(P∨Q)$

II. $P∧¬Q$

III. $¬P∧¬Q$
question.worked_solution:
Two statements are logically equivalent if they have the same truth table. So, we construct a truth table for the three given statements:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬Q∧(P∨Q)\,$ | $\,P∧¬Q\,$ | $\,¬P∧¬Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

We see that only the statements $¬Q∧(P∨Q)$ and $P∧¬Q$ have the same truth table, so they are logically equivalent.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
